conviction_note: Management pre-released the quarter's shape on 2026-09-15 (NII and fees at the upper end of guidance, expenses at the lower end, NCOs mid-range), consensus revenue of $3.34bn already sits at those upper ends, and this name sold a 16% beat with a raised guide in July (-2.29%). So the reported quarter is close to a non-event. What is left is the Q4/2027 guide, a formal synergy raise above $850m, and the size of the Q4 buyback against an AOCI hit from a roughly 85bp Q3 rise in the 10-year. Those roughly offset, with a slight positive lean because the stock fell with a sector de-rating (KRE -4.3% over 20 days against FITB -4.9%) rather than on anything company-specific. abs_move is 3.0: above the name's 1.31% median because a guide and a capital update are both due in a volatile sector tape, but well below the 5.78% option figure, which is inflated by sector IV of 29.8 against 15.7 realised. p_up 53. The findings sum (+0.6) and the scaled number (+0.18) agree in sign and both are small.
bar: Revenue $3.34bn (MarketBeat 2026-10-12 https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-fifth-third-bancorp-fitb-projected-to-post-quarterly-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-12/ and Benzinga, two agreeing sources). Company Q3 guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000035527/000003552726000193/fifththirdbancorppresent.htm, slide 14): NII up 2-2.5% from $2.22bn, i.e. $2.264-2.276bn; fees up 1-3% from $1.04bn, i.e. $1.050-1.071bn; expense down 1-2% from $1.86bn; NCOs 30-35bp. The upper ends of NII plus fees come to about $3.345bn, the same as consensus. The EPS bar is DISPUTED: $0.81-0.88 (MarketBeat $0.826, TipRanks $0.84, Benzinga $0.81/$0.88, apparently GAAP-like after merger charges) against about $1.08 adjusted (Earnings Whispers, sweep). So EPS-based sizes are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 36.3M shares on the 2026-09-30 settlement, up from 32.2M on 09-15 (about 4.0% of shares out), days to cover 5.0 (FINRA via https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/fitb/short-interest/, read 2026-10-16). Moderate and not crowded. 25-delta skew +0.77 vol points, which is close to flat; put/call OI 0.42; the baseline's priced lean is 'balanced'. ATM IV 29.8% against 15.7% 20-day realised: the option-implied event move of 5.78% carries sector vol premium and sits far above the 7-print history (median 1.31%, max 2.29%). Sell-side trimmed targets into the print: Truist 64->63 (09-23), Evercore 61->57 (10-01), JPM 62->58 (10-02), UBS 65->63 (10-05).

findings.finding: At the Barclays conference on 2026-09-15 the CFO said Q3 NII and fee income were tracking at the UPPER end of guidance (NII +2.5% to about $2.276bn, fees +3% to about $1.07bn), expenses at the LOWER end (-2% to about $1.82bn), NCOs mid-range (about 30-32bp against a 30-35bp guide) and NIM 'sticks in the mid-330s'. That arithmetic gives adjusted EPS of about $1.10 against the about $1.08 adjusted consensus, and revenue of about $3.345bn against a $3.34bn consensus, so the bar has already absorbed the pre-announcement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-17): adjusted EPS $1.02 against about $0.88, with NII and fee guidance raised, and the stock fell 2.29%. The other six prints moved between -1.0% and +1.95%. Beats on this line have not paid.
findings.why_not_priced: It largely is priced. The update was public, and the $3.34bn revenue consensus equals the upper ends of NII plus fees. If it were not priced, consensus revenue would sit near the guide midpoint (about $3.32bn). A small residual remains only if the print lands above the upper end.
findings.independence: MarketBeat/Yahoo write-up of the same remarks (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/fifth-third-sees-q3-high-030202045.html, 2026-09-20). Same event and same document, so it counts once.

findings.finding: Long rates rose sharply in Q3 2026: the 10-year was 5.11% on 2026-09-23, and a WSJ summary put the quarter's rise at about 85bp, the largest since 2016. Peers that have reported show the tangible-book hit: Regions TBVPS fell 8.2% q/q ($13.78 to $12.65), Citizens fell 6.6% ($38.29 to $35.78, which it attributed to 'higher long-term rates on the investment securities and swap portfolios'), and Citizens cut its Q3 buyback to $125m from $225m. FITB entered Q3 with a $2.9bn after-tax unrealized loss and CET1 including AOCI of about 8.7%, while regulatory CET1 was 9.9% against a 10-10.5% target. FITB's own 6/30 slide projected AOCI improving to -$2.7bn by year-end, which the rate move reverses. The Street expects a $200-300m Q4 buyback, and the risk is that the call delays or shrinks it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved FITB print in the baseline turned on capital return; buybacks were paused all of H1 2026 after the Comerica close. Peers on the same AOCI line this week: Regions +2.3% on its print with TBV -8.2% and a $95m buyback; Citizens about -1.0% intraday with TBV -6.6% and a smaller buyback.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The sector TBV hit has been visible in peer prints since 10-15/16, and FITB moved with KRE. What is not visible is FITB's own Q4 buyback decision. If the market expected a cut, the $200-300m buyback estimate would have been pulled, and the stock would have lagged KRE more than 0.6 points over 20 days. Counterweight: the COO said on 09-15 'we'll be back to a more normalized share repurchase program in the fourth quarter', when the 10-year was already about 5.0%, so management spoke with most of the rate move known. That is why the size is small.
findings.independence: Regions TBV figures (https://doingmoretoday.com/regions-reports-third-quarter-2026-earnings/, 2026-10-16); FITB AOCI slide and 6/30 unrealized loss (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000035527/000003552726000193/fifththirdbancorppresent.htm); CET1 including AOCI 8.7% and the $200-300m Q4 buyback expectation (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/01/fifth-third-raises-dividend-while-walking-capital-tightrope-post-comerica-deal/, 2026-10-01); 10-year 5.11% on 09-23 (Treasury par curve, via search). The FITB-specific transmission is inference from peers.

findings.finding: Peer read-across from this week is benign on NII and credit: Regions NII +2% q/q with NCOs down to 29bp from 42bp and criticized loans and NPLs both lower; Citizens NII +2.7% q/q with NCOs stable at 37bp and CET1 up to 10.5%; PNC's adjusted EPS of $5.09 came with higher NII and lower expenses. Deposit-cost drift after the September hike was small (Regions interest-bearing deposit costs +1bp, Citizens +5bp). Same-day stock reactions were mixed: USB +2.0% (10-15), PNC -0.4% while KRE rose 1.8% (10-15), RF +2.3%, TFC +1.1%, CFG -1.0% and MTB -2.7% intraday on 10-16.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FITB's own credit line has been quiet since the 2025 Tricolor impairment ($170-200m, Q3 2025); Q2 2026 NCOs of 30bp were the lowest since 2Q23, and the stock still fell on that print.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Peers printed before FITB and the market has read them. The small positive is that no peer flagged an NDFI or CRE credit event that would read across to FITB's $13.1bn NDFI book or Comerica's middle-market loans. If a peer had, KRE would have sold off on 10-15/16 rather than rising 1.8% on 10-15.
findings.independence: Citizens release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000759944/000075994426000206/a3q26earningsrelease.htm); PNC 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000713676/000162828026065936/q32026financialhighlightsa.htm); Yahoo chart closes for USB, PNC, CFG, TFC, MTB and KRE, read 2026-10-16. Citizens shares the AOCI document with finding 2, but this finding rests on a different line (NII and credit).

findings.finding: The Comerica systems conversion (about 600,000 accounts, 293 branches, Labor Day weekend 2026) produced local-news reports on 2026-09-08/09 of login lockouts, bill-pay outages of up to eight days, cancelled autopays and long hold times in Michigan and Texas. A week later management said it was 'as close to perfect as I have seen', with inbound calls 15% below the MB Financial conversion, commercial gross attrition under 1%, consumer attrition 'very stable and very muted', and 'quite a strong quarter' for deposit growth. Q3 period-end deposits and retention figures will show which account holds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior FITB print turned on deposit attrition; Q2 commercial retention was 99.4% and the stock fell 2.29% on other lines.
findings.why_not_priced: Both sides are public: the glitches were in Detroit media and management's rebuttal came at a conference. The complaints are anecdotal and uncounted. Only a visible deposit outflow from legacy Comerica markets would be new, and management's 09-15 deposit comment argues against one. Net zero.
findings.independence: Detroit News (https://www.detroitnews.com/story/business/2026/09/08/fifth-thirds-comerica-conversion-brings-access-problems-for-customers/91664860007/) on the negative side; the Barclays transcript (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/fifth-third-at-barclays-conference-comerica-deal-lifts-growth-plans-93CH-4901613) on the positive side. Opposing sources.

findings.finding: Cost synergies are running above the formal target: on 2026-09-15 the COO said 'we hit the $850 million' and the CFO said 'we're probably north of $900 million at this point'. Management also guides to more than $500m of revenue synergies over 3-5 years and a 53% efficiency target for 2027. The Q3 call is the first with the conversion done, so a formal raise of the $850m run-rate target and a first 2027 expense outlook are likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 raised NII and fee guidance and cut expense guidance, and the stock fell 2.29%, so guide raises on this name have not reliably paid.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced, since the 'north of $900m' remark is public. Not formalised: aggregator descriptions and the 2026-09-20 MarketBeat write-up still carry the $850m target. If the Street had fully adopted about $900m-plus, the FY2027 EPS consensus of $4.96 would already reflect roughly $50m of extra after-tax savings (about $0.05). The 2027 expense guide has never been given.
findings.independence: MarketBeat/Yahoo (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/fifth-third-sees-q3-high-030202045.html) repeats the same remark, so this is one document. Finding 1 also rests on this transcript, but on a different line (the quarter rather than the forward guide).

findings.finding: FITB goes into the print on a sector de-rating, not a company-specific one. The KBW Bank Index fell 13% from mid-August and September was financials' worst month against the S&P 500 since 1990, which Truist's Foran attributed to fund flows rather than results. Over 20 sessions FITB fell 4.9% against KRE's 4.3%, and it is 15% off its 52-week high. Four sell-side target cuts landed 09-23 to 10-05 with no rating changes. Short interest rose 13% in the second half of September, to 36.3M shares (5.0 days to cover).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior FITB print came into a comparable sector drawdown in the baseline window. Peers this week coming off the same drawdown were mixed on the day (RF +2.3%, USB +2.0%, TFC +1.1%, PNC -0.4%, CFG -1.0%, MTB -2.7%).
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself: the drawdown is the market's view. The lean is only that a clean print and a buyback restart can relieve a flow-driven discount. Against it, peers this week did not bounce on clean prints, so the size is small.
findings.independence: KRE and FITB closes from the Yahoo chart (read 2026-10-16); short interest from FINRA via https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/fitb/short-interest/; target cuts from MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-fifth-third-bancorp-fitb-projected-to-post-quarterly-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-12/).

findings.finding: Industry commercial loan demand is strong: the Fed's H.8 shows C&I loans growing about 18.8% annualized in August 2026 (12.0% July, 14.8% June) and bank credit about 4.8%. FITB guided Q3 average loans to only +1% and on 09-15 said loans were 'coming in as expected' and Comerica loans 'relatively stable'. FITB's middle-market sales force is 75% larger after Comerica, so there is scope for a firmer Q4 loan guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Loan growth has not been the line FITB's reactions were attributed to in the resolved prints.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an industry series with no company confirmation, and the company itself said loans were only 'as expected', which caps it. If the market expected FITB to capture that growth, FY2027 estimates would have moved up through September; instead targets were cut.
findings.independence: This is a proxy; the company's 09-15 'as expected' points the other way, toward zero (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/fifth-third-at-barclays-conference-comerica-deal-lifts-growth-plans-93CH-4901613).

findings.finding: Q3 NIM will be flat or down against Q2's 3.36%: management said it 'sticks in the mid-330s' because cash balances ran 'north of $20 billion' for most of the quarter. Contributors were about $2bn of Comerica sweep balances placed on deposit during the transition and a Southwest deposit campaign that beat its $2.5bn target by more than double; promotional deposits are higher-cost funding. The 3.40% exit-rate target therefore rests on Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 NIM rose 6bp to 3.36% and the stock still fell 2.29%; Truist was 'dinged on NIM concern' in Q2 per Zacks, so the sector does punish NIM misses.
findings.why_not_priced: The flat NIM is guided and public. The residual is whether the Q4 NIM and deposit-cost guide holds the 3.40% exit after the September hike: Citizens' interest-bearing deposit costs rose 5bp in Q3.
findings.independence: Same transcript as findings 1 and 5, but a different line (NIM and funding mix). Citizens' deposit-cost rise (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000759944/000075994426000206/a3q26earningsrelease.htm) is the independent read.

findings.finding: Liability housekeeping in the quarter: a registered exchange of $1.27bn of Comerica-era restricted senior notes (4.000% 2029 and 5.982% FtF 2030) settled about 2026-09-24 with 99.9%+ tendered and no P&L effect stated, and the full $500m 1.707% FtF senior notes due 2027 are called at par for 2026-11-01. Asked what the money buys: nothing new. These are a registration change and a routine call of low-coupon paper, funded from the $20bn-plus cash position.
findings.why_not_priced: Immaterial. Filed only for completeness; no line moves on it.

findings.finding: The rate deck has not moved against the guide. FITB's FY and Q3 NII guidance assumed a 4.00% fed funds rate at both 9/30 and 12/31, and the upper bound was 4.00% on 2026-09-30 after the September hike. FITB is mildly asset-sensitive (+0.4% NII in year 1 and +1.9% in year 2 for +100bp). Higher long rates lift fixed-rate asset repricing, which Regions and Citizens both cited as a NII driver. Together that is a modest tailwind for the 2027 NII outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 NII guide raise was sold (-2.29%).
findings.why_not_priced: This is macro-to-company inference; the company has not updated its 2027 view. The same rate move drives the AOCI negative in finding 2, so the two partly offset by design: NII up, capital down.
findings.independence: Fed funds upper bound of 4.00% at 9/30 (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/01/fifth-third-raises-dividend-while-walking-capital-tightrope-post-comerica-deal/); Citizens citing fixed-rate asset repricing (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000759944/000075994426000206/a3q26earningsrelease.htm). Proxy.

outside_window.finding: Comerica wealth-platform conversion scheduled for Halloween (2026-10-31) and HR systems for 2027-01-01; any disruption there lands after the exit window.
Next FOMC meeting on 2026-10-27/28, with the market pricing a low (about 19%) probability of another hike; this would move FITB's rate assumptions only after the window.

baseline_tension: Neither cuts hard against the baseline: the skew is near flat (+0.77) and the lean balanced, and FITB's 20-day fall matches the sector rather than any company news. My slight positive lean on a clean print and a buyback restart therefore runs mildly against the run-up only, and it is sized small because this name has sold its last beat and guide raise.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar disputed, finding inside the guide): the EPS bar is $0.81-0.88 against $1.08 and the pre-announced upper ends are already in revenue consensus, so finding 1 went from 0.3 to 0.1 and print_vs_bar from 0.5 to 0.3
